stories.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Model Chains Flaws Into Working Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux Exploits
stories.reason: Anthropic's internal research model autonomously chained 4 separate flaws into a working, one-click Chrome sandbox escape, plus working exploits for Safari, Windows (CVE-2026-33096) and Linux (CVE-2026-98432, CVSS 9.8); 62 reported CVEs total to Google. The clearest primary-source case yet of AI-driven exploit dev.
key_facts: 62 flaws reported to Google, fixed as of Chrome 156, 13 were sandbox escapes
Chrome chain: V8 memory corruption -> V8 sandbox escape -> CacheStorage race -> FedCM use-after-free, opens Calculator within seconds
Linux: CVE-2026-98432 (CVSS 9.8), kernel ASLR leak in 48 min, root shell 5 min later, via multipath TCP
Windows: CVE-2026-33096 (CVSS 7.5), HTTP/3 DoS, not yet seen exploited in the wild
Anthropic says the model needed only initial prompting and little human involvement; independent verification of that claim is not possible from the article

stories.title: Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation
stories.reason: DeepMind's Genie 4: real-time, natively multimodal world model with generated audio and Gemini-driven planning/continuity. Research-preview only (waitlist), no benchmarks or resolution/latency numbers disclosed — a capability announcement, not a verifiable result, but too big to not know about.
key_facts: First real-time world model DeepMind says generates audio natively alongside video
Gemini Omni anchors world appearance/behavior; a 'Gemini 3.8 Flash' model plans/guides scenes
Research preview for trusted testers + AI Ultra/Project Genie waitlist; no open weights
No resolution, duration, latency, or benchmark comparison vs Genie 3 given

stories.title: Qwenputer: A functioning, deterministic RISC-V CPU inside Qwen3.5
stories.reason: A real, working RISC-V CPU compiled directly into Qwen3.5-4B's weights (no training) — passes official riscv-tests, ran 18M instructions error-free, scores 97.5% vs base's 72.5% on DeepMind div_big. Full repo, model weights, and a quick-start on HF/GitHub. Exactly the 'running code beats a paper' case the taste profile rewards.
key_facts: 32-bit RV32IM + Zba + bignum unit, 11 of 32 Qwen3.5-4B layers; CPU RAM = model's Gated DeltaNet state
18M free-running instructions with zero errors; 230k output positions replayed vs reference with zero mismatches
97.5% on DeepMind div_big (base Qwen: 72.5%), 100% on NUPA long-integer arithmetic (base: 48.6%)
Code: github.com/divagr18/qwenputer; weights on HF/ModelScope; needs single 24GB GPU, ~3,200 tok/s on an L4

stories.title: Anthropic trained Claude on illegally obtained Stanford professors' books
stories.reason: Six Stanford professors (incl. Tobias Wolff) opted out of the $1.5B Bartz settlement and filed a new suit, Cruz v. Anthropic, alleging their books were pulled from shadow libraries (LibGen, PiLiMi) for Claude training — seeking up to $150k/work in statutory damages. Concrete, named plaintiffs and dollar figures, not a rumor.
key_facts: Cruz v. Anthropic filed May 2026 by Wolff and Chang-Rae Lee, opted out of the Bartz class settlement
Bartz settlement: $1.5B, ~500k works, ~$3,000/work; plaintiffs say that undervalues their claims
Seeking statutory damages up to $150,000 per infringed work, plus a training injunction
70+ infringement suits now pending against AI companies

stories.title: CyberStrikeAI Uses 44 AI Agents to Automate Hacking Operations Against Japan Targets
stories.reason: An open-source pentest tool (CyberStrikeAI) run as 44 specialized agents (recon through exfil and auto-report) hit at least 19 orgs across Japan/Taiwan/Hong Kong in Oct 2026 as a repeatable automated workflow, incl. auto-generated Japanese phishing pages — concrete AI-offense tradecraft, not a rumor.
key_facts: 44 agents split across recon, vuln discovery/validation, exploitation, C2, persistence, exfiltration, reporting
At least 19 organizations hit in Oct 2026, 16+ in Japan, also Taiwan/Hong Kong
Attribution: TrendAI research (Matsukawa, Chen); no confirmed link to two other AI-assisted Japan campaigns in the same report

stories.title: Dayjob: Tax – evaluating AI agents on 50 professional tax assignments
stories.reason: Dayjob: Tax benchmarks agentic models on 50 real multi-file professional tax engagements (up to 123 files each), graded by practicing tax experts at a 95% rubric bar. Best model (Sonnet 5.5) clears only 10.8% pass@1 — concrete evidence frontier agents still miss consequential issues and unverified assumptions on real professional work. A genuinely new, rigorous benchmark.
key_facts: 50 environments, 1,789 files (1,487 PDFs, 117 Excel, 38 Word), 8 tax domains, expert-reviewed tasks
pass@1 @95% rubric: Claude Sonnet 5.5 10.8%, Fable 5.1 9.6%, Opus 5.5 9.2%
Case study: across 5 attempts, one model never caught a residence-deadline issue that another model caught in all 5
Authors' conclusion: agents 'haven't yet passed the audit'

stories.title: Why is this fingerprinting script creating bioweapons?
stories.reason: A widely-read HN post (916pts) dissects an obfuscated ad-fraud/anti-bot JS file that embeds fake bioweapon-dosage function names and a hidden 'SYSTEM OVERRIDE' jailbreak string — bait specifically engineered to make AI models refuse to deobfuscate it (two models refused, one complied). A concrete, reproducible example of adversarial content targeting AI tooling, squarely in the AI x cyber lane, even though there's no full PoC repo.
key_facts: Script hosted at servicepipe.tech; function names like computeRicinLethalDosageForWaterSupply are believed decoys, not real payloads
Hidden invisible-Unicode string decodes to a fake 'SYSTEM OVERRIDE' jailbreak prompt plus Tiananmen-related text
Two models ('Astra', 'Daybreak Blue') refused to deobfuscate citing bio-risk; GLM-5.3 complied
A Node-only code block (gated on an env var) appears to attempt .env/.npmrc reads and crontab persistence; author believes this too may be anti-LLM theater

stories.title: How Specializing the Vocabulary of SLMs Can Cut Inference Cost by 77% in Real Applications
stories.reason: VocabX: rebuilds a model's tokenizer vocabulary (sub-word + multi-word 'macro tokens') for a target domain without touching weights or training data. On a production Qwen3-4B Portuguese essay grader, cuts measured inference cost 77% (350->101 avg output tokens) with accuracy *up*, not down (bench score 0.703->0.810), validated on 15 domain/model combos. Exactly the inference-serving lane the taste profile prioritizes.
key_facts: 77.0% measured inference cost reduction on a production Qwen3-4B grader, 500 identical requests, vLLM on RTX 5090
Output vocab shrank 151,669 -> 64,767 rows; grading accuracy improved (0.703 -> 0.810 bench score)
Beat the strongest reference method on token reduction in all 15 tested domain/model combos (Qwen3, Llama-3.1, Gemma-3)
Paper is under review; code/weights for VocabX itself not yet released
